investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official homepage, its full events listing page, one event detail page, and that event's per-event ICS ('Add to Calendar') file. Same AEG-operated venue CMS platform already investigated for verti-music-hall-berlin-01 (same URL/markup pattern), independently confirmed here rather than assumed.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's official events listing page (https://www.uber-arena.de/events/all) immediately exposed 134 distinct upcoming event entries as fully server-rendered static HTML: each event card carries a structured date, category, title, 'starting from' price, and a stable detail-page URL encoding the event slug and start datetime. One sampled event detail page confirmed the same fields plus a discoverable per-event ICS link, whose retained content additionally states an explicit GEO coordinate and street-address LOCATION for the event — richer than the sibling investigation verti-music-hall-berlin-01, and directly usable for venue_location. No JSON-LD, WordPress, Fourvenues, or Sanity signal was present, and none was needed.

venue_reference: Uber Arena (formerly Mercedes-Benz Arena Berlin, renamed 2024; large multipurpose arena, Uber-Platz, Friedrichshain, Berlin)

identity.notes: The retained homepage's own <title> reads 'Uber Arena' and the page repeatedly self-identifies via AEG/Anschutz operator markers, at the venue's own domain uber-arena.de. The retained event ICS also independently states 'in die Uber Arena nach Berlin' in its own description text and a LOCATION of '12 Mühlenstraße Berlin Berlin 10243', matching the arena's known Friedrichshain address — a second, independent confirmation of identity from a distinct retained artifact (not merely the homepage).

site_classification.platform: Custom AEG Presents Europe venue CMS (the same platform family as verti-music-hall-berlin-01/uber-eats-music-hall.de) — server-rendered event listing and detail pages. No WordPress, JSON-LD, Fourvenues, or Sanity signal detected on any fetched page. Each event detail page links a per-event ICS ('Add to Calendar') file, generated server-side and readable without JS; unlike the Music Hall sibling site, this venue's ICS output additionally carries GEO/LOCATION fields.

title.notes:
The listing card's own

...

and the detail page's

Bryan Adams in der Uber Arena

both state the title directly; the shorter 'Bryan Adams' listing-page form is used as the sampled value, matching the source's own primary event-name field (the detail-page h1 additionally appends the venue name, an source-authored variant of the same fact).

start_date.notes: Each event's own structured date markup states weekday, day, month, and year together in one place per event ('Freitag, 02.10.2026'), corroborated by the per-event ICS DTSTART (20261002T180000Z). No cross-record combination needed.

time.notes: The HTML states a floating local time text ('20:00 Uhr', Europe/Berlin) directly on the same event card/detail page as the title. The per-event ICS DTSTART independently and directly states the same instant as a full UTC timestamp (20261002T180000Z = 20:00 CEST). Recorded value is the ICS's own explicit UTC instant.

end.notes: The HTML never states an end time (only a start time and, separately, a doors/'Einlass' time). The per-event ICS carries a DTEND, but it is exactly DTSTART+2h (20:00Z) — the same fixed-default-duration pattern already observed for verti-music-hall-berlin-01's two sampled events, not a genuine venue-stated end time. Not promoted to a proven fact.

venue_location.notes: Unlike verti-music-hall-berlin-01, this source's per-event ICS directly states its own LOCATION ('12 Mühlenstraße  Berlin Berlin 10243') and GEO ('52.5063462;13.4436582') fields on every VEVENT — a genuinely per-record, directly-stated fact, not inherited from page context. The HTML event cards themselves do not restate the venue name, but the ICS (fetched per event, same Level-1 static acquisition) does.

source_record_id.notes: Each event's own detail-page URL path (slug + start-datetime suffix) is the site's own canonical, directly-stated permalink for that specific occurrence — the same documented URL-slug stable-identifier strategy already used for moog-barcelona-01/LAV and for the sibling investigation verti-music-hall-berlin-01. A secondary numeric CMS id is also directly observable in the event's own ICS link path ('/events/ical/bryan-adams-berlin/3772/1'), corroborating a stable platform-internal id.

event_url.notes: Each event card's own detail-page link, stated directly.

price.notes: Each listing card shows only an 'ab' (starting-from) price string per event (e.g. 'ab 60,00 €') — a real, directly-stated value, but a lower-bound indicator rather than a complete price/tier breakdown, so not promoted to a single proven price value.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from two independently retained artifacts (homepage title/operator markers, and the ICS's own description/LOCATION text).

source_record_id PROVEN via the site's own slug+datetime permalink path, following the documented moog-barcelona-01/LAV precedent.
